course.title: Go (Golang) — From Beginner to Professional
course.description: A visual-first course for the Go language, from environment setup and syntax through data structures, interfaces, generics, testing, concurrency, HTTP APIs, SQL persistence, performance, security, deployment, and professional engineering.
course.version_scope: Technical baseline: Go 1.27.2 was listed by the official Go release history as released on 2026-10-08 and is used as the current reference baseline for this curriculum snapshot dated 2026-10-17. Stable language and standard-library topics are separated from version-specific Go 1.27 features (generic methods, encoding/json/v2 and uuid) and optional experimental SIMD/cgo/unsafe/assembly topics. Re-check official Go release history and security announcements before publication; code samples have not been executed in a Go 1.27 runtime in this build environment.
audience: developers preparing to build APIs, CLIs, network services, cloud applications, or systems software
prerequisites: No prior Go knowledge is required. Learners should be comfortable using a computer and managing files and folders. Basic programming logic is helpful but not mandatory.
learning_outcomes: Write formatted and idiomatic Go programs using the language fundamentals.
Organize packages and modules and manage dependencies intentionally.
Use data structures, methods, interfaces, and generics to build reusable components.
Handle errors, test behavior, debug defects, and measure performance.
Use goroutines, channels, synchronization, and cancellation to coordinate concurrent work safely.
Build HTTP clients and services and persist data through appropriate SQL abstractions.
Apply secure coding, dependency checks, observability, deployment, and maintenance practices.
